messages:
Raj (Support): heads up — received an escalation from a customer (Tessera) at 09:13 UTC in eu-west-4. They report a sudden spike of 502/timeout errors across hosted inference endpoints. Sample from their side: curl -> 502, 0 bytes on response. Can we triage?

Elena (CS): they pasted latency graphs — 99p token latency jumped and request rate stayed normal. They think it started ~09:12 and some calls show TCP RST. Really hurting their users.

Sara (SRE): on it. Can you drop the raw request IDs + one example curl? Also what region/az prefix?

Raj (Support): sent logs + example: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood-hosted.com/v1/generate \n* Connected to api.redwood-hosted.com (35.XXX.XXX.XX) port 443 (#0)\n> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1\n> ...\n< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\n< content-length: 0\n```

Mike (Netops): pinging their path from eu-west-4b probe now. putting mtr running.

Mike (Netops): pasted MTR (shortened):
```
# mtr -r -c 40 api.redwood-hosted.com
1. gw.local 0.2%
2. mid-hop 0.5%
3. transit-provider-1 21.7%  <-- intermittent loss
4. provider-edge 18.9%
5. our-euw4b-edge 0.0%
```

Sara (SRE): 20% loss at provider hop 3 — that explains packet retransmits and 502s when backend TCP times out. Is this localized to eu-west-4b or cross-az?

Mike (Netops): running cross-AZ checks — eu-west-4a probes show 0% to same peer. Looks like the path into 4b from provider X is degrading. BGP table looks stable, no local flaps.

deploy-bot: deploy 17694abcd completed in eu-west-4b at 09:05 UTC.

Sara (SRE): could be provider-side microbursts or policing on that POP. Quick mitigation: shift incoming gateway traffic for hosted inference away from eu-west-4b to eu-west-4a via router-policy, and enable fallback routing for customer tessera to the A zone to avoid in-flight requests restarting. I can put a temporary route preference.

Raj (Support): I told Tessera we're investigating and asked them to retry on fallback zone; they'll accept routing change but asked for ETA.

Mike (Netops): opened ticket with transit provider (ticket 456789). Noted high packet loss on hop 3 towards eu-west-4b. Asked for immediate edge check and whether they have shaping, queue drops.

transit-bot: provider acked ticket 456789, investigating (ref 789-RT).

Sara (SRE): action list: 1) apply route preference to shift traffic off 4b (I can do that), 2) add health-based routing on gateway to prefer eu-west-4a while loss > 2%, 3) monitor customer error rates and SLO. Any objections?

Mike (Netops): +1. I'll also add a quick ACL workaround for the provider pop to force new flows via a different next-hop if possible.

Elena (CS): Please flag if we need to proactively credit tessera — they hit 12 minutes of 5xx peak. I'll draft message once we have recovery window.

Sara (SRE): making the route change now — switching 30% of gateway traffic to eu-west-4a, enabling sticky fallback for in-flight sessions.

Sara (SRE): done. Monitoring logs.

~09:34 UTC~
Mike (Netops): provider reverted a config at their edge, loss dropped to <0.5% on probe. MTR now:
```
1. gw.local 0.0%
2. mid-hop 0.0%
3. transit-provider-1 0.4%
4. provider-edge 0.0%
5. our-euw4b-edge 0.0%
```

Raj (Support): customer confirms traffic is healthy again and 502s cleared around 09:36 UTC. They still saw elevated latencies for a bit but back to normal.

Sara (SRE): rolling update: root cause appears to be transient packet loss at provider edge into eu-west-4b causing TCP retransmits and backend timeouts => 502s at gateway. Recovery after provider changed config. Immediate mitigations we used: route preference + gateway health fallback.

Mike (Netops): provider said they had an egress queue misconfiguration during a micro-deployment at their POP. They fixed it, will send RCA.

Elena (CS): I'll send Tessera a post-incident note, offer 1 day credit, and explain mitigation steps. Please add short summary for the customer with timeline + what we did.

Sara (SRE): follow-ups: (a) add automatic health-based route preference to move traffic off an AZ if provider loss > 2% for 3m, (b) add a synthetic probe from multiple provider POPs into each AZ to detect provider-side micros, (c) include this pattern in runbook for packet-loss -> 502. I'll put tasks in backlog.

Raj (Support): thanks everyone. Saving logs and linking to ticket 456789. Will add customer timeline and mark as resolved after provider RCA.

transit-bot: ticket 456789 updated by provider: investigating config change, ETA for RCA 24h.

Sara (SRE): closing thread for now — will reopen if we see reoccurrence. Postmortem to be scheduled.

Elena (CS): noted, will follow up with Tessera. :thumbsup:
